newsitem.title: USA: Bear Stearns faces new twist in probe - NYT.
newsitem.headline: Bear Stearns faces new twist in probe - NYT.

text.p: A Bear Stearns Cos Inc employee has said that an executive in the firm told him to destroy documents connected to an investigation into the firm's dealings with the defunct A.R. Baron & Co, the New York Times said.
In Tuesday's edition, the Times said that correspondence between lawyers in the firm do not identify the executive or the complaining employee, but indicate that the executive is a managing director.

Since the collapse of Baron last year, Bear Stearns has been asked to provide information to the New York County District Attorney and the New York State Attorney General, federal and industry regulators and lawyers for Baron's creditors.
Baron filed for bankruptcy in 1996 and is being liquidated. Bear Stearns processed trades for Baron.
Mark Lehman, an executive president and chief counsel for Bear Stearns, confirmed that the firm knew about the employee's accusation.

"We have heard of such allegations; we have discovered that allegation," Lehman said. "We have reported it immediately to the appropriate law enforcement authorities. We continue to cooperate with law enforcement in all regards."
Lehman said the firm expects to be able to comply with "any appropriate requests for relevant information."
